tool_arguments.query: Marvell Technology custom AI silicon revenue Q3 fiscal 2026 data center

events.content: Marvell Technology custom AI silicon revenue Q3 fiscal 2026 data center

Marvell generated **$1.518 billion of data-center revenue in Q3 fiscal 2026** (three months ended **November 1, 2025**), up **38% year over year** from $1.101 billion and **2% sequentially** from $1.491 billion. [[1]] 

Data center represented **73% of Marvell’s $2.075 billion total Q3 revenue**, making it the company’s dominant end market. [[1]] 

The quarterly increase was approximately **$27.4 million sequentially**, while the year-over-year increase was approximately **$416.8 million**, based on Marvell’s reported end-market revenue figures. [[1]] 

Marvell does **not** disclose separate Q3 revenue amounts for **custom AI silicon** versus **electro-optics**; it reports their contribution within the aggregate data-center end market rather than as standalone product-revenue lines. [[1]] 

Management had identified strong AI demand for both custom silicon and electro-optics as a key growth driver entering Q3, and stated that custom-AI design activity had reached an all-time high, with more than 50 opportunities across over 10 customers. [[2]] 

Total Q3 revenue of **$2.075 billion** exceeded the midpoint of Marvell’s prior **$2.060 billion ±5%** guidance by **$15 million**, while the company guided Q4 fiscal 2026 revenue to **$2.200 billion ±5%**. [[1]] [[2]] [[1]]

Sources:

tool_arguments.query: Marvell Technology data center revenue split custom AI silicon electro-optics fiscal 2025 fiscal 2026

events.content: Marvell Technology data center revenue split custom AI silicon electro-optics fiscal 2025 fiscal 2026

Marvell did **not disclose a Q1 FY2026 revenue split between custom AI silicon and electro-optics**, so an exact dollar or percentage allocation cannot be reliably calculated from its reported results. [[1]] 

The company reported **$1.4406 billion** of data-center revenue for the quarter ended **May 3, 2025**, equal to **76% of total company revenue**, with total revenue of **$1.895 billion**. [[1]] 

Management attributed data-center momentum to both the rapid scaling of custom-silicon programs and robust electro-optics shipments, but provided no component-level revenue figures or mix percentages for either category. [[1]] 

Thus, the defensible Q1 FY2026 “split” is: **Data center: $1.441 billion; custom AI silicon: not separately disclosed; electro-optics: not separately disclosed; residual data-center products: also not separately disclosed.** [[1]] 

Qualitatively, management indicated that its lead hyperscaler XPU program had become a key custom-business revenue driver and that optics was performing well and expected to grow during the year, but these comments do not establish a quarterly revenue mix. [[2]]

**Marvell Technology — Q2 FY2027 AI/Data-Center read-through:** Marvell reported record Q2 FY2027 revenue of **$2.739 billion** for the quarter ended **August 1, 2026**, up **37% year over year** and **13% sequentially**; GAAP diluted EPS was **$0.33** and non-GAAP diluted EPS was **$0.94**. [[1]]

**Data center was the central driver:** Data-center revenue reached **$2.172 billion**, up **46% YoY** and **18% QoQ**, and represented **79%** of company revenue, versus 74% a year earlier. [[2]] This implies that virtually all of Marvell’s near-term growth thesis is now linked to hyperscale AI infrastructure rather than its communications-and-other businesses. [[2]]

**Guidance moved materially higher:** Management guided Q3 FY2027 revenue to **$3.15 billion ±5%**, which at the midpoint implies roughly **15% sequential growth** and more than **50% YoY growth**; it also raised FY2027 revenue expectations to approximately **$12 billion** and FY2028 expectations to approximately **$18 billion**. [[2]] [[3]] Management expects data-center revenue to grow about **60% in FY2027** and more than **60% in FY2028**. [[4]] [[3]]

**Custom AI silicon is shifting from design-win narrative to revenue ramp:** Marvell said its Custom business should accelerate significantly in the second half of FY2027, with growth coming from both **XPU** programs and **XPU-attach** products, including custom NICs and CXL-related products. [[1]] [[4]] The disclosed expanded hyperscaler warrant agreement covers existing custom programs, new design wins, and potential future programs spanning AI inference accelerators, storage controllers, NICs, memory-interface controllers, and near-memory compute. [[4]] The important investment implication is that custom silicon can add a second major AI engine alongside connectivity, but it may also pressure gross margin as its revenue mix rises. [[4]] [[3]]

**Electro-optics/connectivity remains the nearer-term revenue base:** Marvell cited strong demand across connectivity, including **800G and 1.6T scale-out optics**, **51.2T Ethernet switches**, scale-up optical solutions for **NPO/CPO**, and coherent **1.6T ZR/ZR+** modules for data-center interconnect. [[5]] [[6]] Management said 800G demand remains strong, 1.6T is ramping rapidly, and 51.2T products are expected to drive more than a doubling of scale-out-switching revenue during FY2027. [[6]]

events.content: Marvell Technology data center revenue FY2026 full year custom AI silicon electro optics split

Marvell’s FY2026 ended January 31, 2026, and generated $8.195 billion of total revenue; management said data-center revenue “surpassed $6 billion,” up 46% year over year. [[1]] [[2]]

| FY2026 data-center revenue split | Revenue / share |
|---|---:|
| Optical interconnect / optics | **Roughly half of data-center revenue**, implying **just over ~$3.0 billion** |
| Custom silicon | **~$1.5 billion**, or **approximately 25%** of data-center revenue |
| Other data-center products—e.g., switching, storage, and remaining interconnect | **Roughly 25%**, implying **about ~$1.5 billion-plus** |

Marvell’s own proxy describes optical interconnect as “roughly half” of FY2026 data-center revenue and custom silicon as “approximately 25%”; therefore, these are management-reported mix percentages rather than a formally disclosed, exact audited product-revenue table. [[3]] 

The custom-silicon figure is the clearest absolute disclosure: management said custom revenue doubled year over year to **$1.5 billion** in FY2026. [[2]] 

Accordingly, the practical FY2026 **custom silicon vs. optics split** is approximately **$1.5 billion custom / >$3.0 billion optics**, or about **25% / 50%** of the data-center business, respectively. [[3]]

- Marvell reported record Q1 FY2027 revenue of **$2.418 billion**, up **28% year over year** and **9% sequentially**. [[2]]

- The remaining **communications and other** revenue was **$585.1 million**, up **29% year over year** and **3% sequentially**. [[4]] [[2]]
- Q1 profitability included a **52.1% GAAP gross margin**, **58.9% non-GAAP gross margin**, and **$0.80 non-GAAP diluted EPS**. [[5]]

**Custom AI silicon**

- Management said custom-silicon revenue remains on track to grow **more than 20% year over year in FY2027**, led by its flagship XPU program and additional XPU-attach ramps, including CXL and NIC products. [[3]]
- For FY2028, Marvell forecast custom revenue to grow **more than 100% year over year**, driven by multiple program ramps and several new custom design wins. [[2]]
- This implies the Q1 data-center performance was not dependent on a single product category: management reported sequential and annual growth across **optical interconnect, custom silicon, and switching**. [[3]]

**Electro-optics / interconnect**

- Marvell raised its FY2027 interconnect-revenue growth outlook to **more than 70% year over year**, making interconnect the principal source of the expected approximately **50% FY2027 data-center-revenue growth**. [[2]] [[3]]
- Demand cited by the company spans **800G and 1.6T scale-out optics**, **51.2T Ethernet scale-out switches**, scale-up optical solutions for **NPO/CPO**, and scale-across data-center-interconnect modules. [[4]]
- The scale-up-optics opportunity is expected to ramp strongly in FY2028, with revenue forecast to more than double versus the company’s prior **approximately $150 million** outlook. [[2]]
- Scale-out-switch revenue is forecast to exceed **$600 million in FY2027**, about double year over year, with a path to approximately **$1 billion in FY2028**. [[2]]

- Marvell guided Q2 FY2027 revenue to **$2.700 billion ±5%** at the midpoint, or roughly **35% year-over-year growth**. [[4]]

Marvell’s FY2026 ended January 31, 2026, and generated $8.195 billion of total revenue; management said data-center revenue “surpassed $6 billion,” up 46% year over year. [[1]] [[2]]

Marvell’s own proxy describes optical interconnect as “roughly half” of FY2026 data-center revenue and custom silicon as “approximately 25%”; therefore, these are management-reported mix percentages rather than a formally disclosed, exact audited product-revenue table. [[3]] 

The custom-silicon figure is the clearest absolute disclosure: management said custom revenue doubled year over year to **$1.5 billion** in FY2026. [[2]] 

Accordingly, the practical FY2026 **custom silicon vs. optics split** is approximately **$1.5 billion custom / >$3.0 billion optics**, or about **25% / 50%** of the data-center business, respectively. [[3]]
